title: Copilot agent draft publish: the app token that runs gh pr ready needs contents: write, since pull-requests: write alone is rejected
answers: Why does gh pr ready fail with a permission error in the Copilot publish workflow?
Which token permissions are needed to mark a draft PR ready for review?
Why does copilot-review.yml no longer request contents: write?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/copilot-agent.yml:publish-draft, specifically its create-github-app-token step, which scopes the token that `gh pr ready` uses. copilot-review.yml:request-review now declares only pull-requests: write.
Rule: markPullRequestReadyForReview rejects a token that has pull-requests: write alone. The token that marks a PR ready must also carry permission-contents: write, and that grant belongs on the publish step's app token. Keep the workflow-level permissions at `{}` and do not add contents: write to the review-request job.
Symptom: Marking the draft ready failed with a permission error when the token only had pull-requests write. The earlier workaround was contents: write on the review job's GITHUB_TOKEN, which over-granted that job.
Constraints: Applies to mutations that flip draft state. Requesting a review or commenting only needs pull-requests write. The reason is upstream: cli/cli issue 8910, cited in a comment in copilot-agent.yml.
applies: Applies to GitHub Actions steps that call gh pr ready or the markPullRequestReadyForReview mutation with an app or token; not to review requests.
says: The bot hit a permission error while publishing the draft pull request for review.
Why does marking the bot draft pull request ready fail with an access error?
Fix permissions so the automated draft pull request can be marked ready for review.
Publishing draft pull requests fails because the bot token lacks required permissions.
